sam (Product): Quick question — I'm moving my primary residence from Oakland, CA to Seattle, WA on 2026-04-10. What's the impact on the monthly WFH stipend, payroll/state withholding, and benefits? Do I need to file anything now?
olivia (People Ops): Congrats on the move! :tada: Short answers: stipend may be prorated the month you move, state withholding will change (WA has no income tax), and you should update your address in the HR portal ASAP.
ben (HRIS): FYI — our HRIS determines stipend eligibility by 'work location' field. If you switch that to WA before the payroll cutoff, the system will prorate the current month's stipend automatically. Cutoff is the 20th at 11:59pm PT.
carla (Finance): From payroll side: because WA has no state income tax, your state withholding will move to "no state tax" status once we process the address change. Please confirm your move date so we can set the effective date on the payroll change.
sam (Product): Move date is 2026-04-10. If I update after the 20th will it only apply next month? Also curious about health plan network — will that change mid-year?
olivia (People Ops): If you update after the 20th, the change will be effective the next pay period (so stipend proration would be for the following month). Health plan: moving states qualifies as a qualifying life event for some carriers — you can request plan changes mid-cycle. I'll DM you the carrier-specific notes.
ben (HRIS): Action items for you: 1) Update mailing address in the HR portal (Profile > Work Location). 2) Submit the "Location Change" form (linked in People Ops docs). 3) Upload proof of new address if asked (lease, utility). That lets us push the change to payroll and benefits.
carla (Finance): Also note: if you have any CA state tax withholdings from prior pay periods, those will remain for earned income while you were CA-based. We'll update withholding going forward. If you need tax advice for the partial-year residency, we recommend contacting our preferred tax advisor (I can share contact).
olivia (People Ops): One more thing: WFH stipend policy — we pay $60/mo by default. Proration = (days active in that calendar month / total days) * $60, rounded to nearest dollar. If you move midpay-period we follow the HRIS effective date.
sam (Product): Perfect. Please go ahead and start the change — I just updated my profile and submitted the form.
payroll-bot: Ticket #PAY-2026-1149 opened to process state withholding and stipend proration for sam. Estimated completion: 2 business days.
olivia (People Ops): Thanks — I'll confirm once payroll finishes the update and send any carrier guidance for benefits. Ping me if you need relocation paperwork or want to check eligibility for a relocation stipend (company relocation assistance is handled separately and requires manager + People Ops approval). :+1:
